## 🤖 AI review — `ai-review:pass`

> ⚠️ **This PR modifies the AI-review machinery (`.github/`/`scripts/`) — the code review still ran; its honest verdict is `ai-review:pass` (above), but a human must review because a gate cannot certify a change to itself.**
>
> The code-review verdict is reported AS-IS — it is **not** masked as `ai-review:changes` (#596), so a genuine reviewer-requested change on a machinery PR still surfaces distinctly. Auto-merge is held by a SEPARATE human gate instead: the `needs-human-review` label, the `machinery-review-required` check, and `ready-to-merge` staying red (no SHA-bound pass witness is posted for a machinery PR).

### Reviewer
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Correctly narrows the DR-029 born gate to skip merge-inherited DRs (blob identical to a merge parent) while still judging DRs authored during resolution; fails closed on conflicted paths and leaves non-merge commits unchanged, with real-hook tests covering all three cases.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Security (code changed)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: No security issues: shell-hook change is injection-safe, no secrets/deps/network, and the born-gate relaxation is bounded to merges and byte-identical inherited blobs with rejection paths still tested.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Architect (design / scope)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Merge-aware fix to the DR-029 born gate is well-scoped, fails-closed toward checking (invariant 2), reversible without a DR, and covered by real-hook regression tests.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Skeptic (evidence discipline)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Every claim is backed by verifiable proof: the real hook is exercised, the regression test preserves its premise, and reject/skip paths are mutually reinforcing — no unproven claim, false status, or assertion-free test.
findings:
- low packages/minspec/tests/githooks-born-gate-merge.test.ts:126 — Non-blocking completeness nit: case 2's `.toThrow(/DR-091/)` would still match if the fix erroneously also rejected the inherited DR-090 (the message would contain both). The inherit-skip behavior is proven separately by case 1, so the invariant is covered overall, but case 2 alone does not distinguish rejects-authored-only from rejects-everything.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

_Independent fresh-context reviewers (`scripts/review-branch.sh`, no-tools agents reading the diff as untrusted data); each label decided by the deterministic fail-closed gate (`scripts/review-decide.sh`). Posted by `minspec-sdd[bot]` from CI — provenance is the App identity, verified here, not the label alone (#428, #342). Coverage `panel` — voters that ran: **reviewer + security + architect + skeptic**. The combined verdict fails toward `changes` if ANY voter requests changes._

<!-- ai-review-guard:staleness -->
**`ai-review:pass` stripped — new commits (#359).**

new commits were pushed after ai-review:pass — the greenlight is stale. A fresh independent review must re-apply `ai-review:pass` before `ready-to-merge` goes green again.

### Reviewer
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: changes
blocking: 1
summary: Hook logic is right and test 1 is valid, but the two rejection cases assert on stderr via execFileSync's thrown message, which only contains the git command — test 2 will fail CI.
findings:
- blocking packages/minspec/tests/githooks-born-gate-merge.test.ts — it('still rejects a DR genuinely authored inside the merge resolution') → expect(...).toThrow(/DR-091/) — execFileSync's thrown Error.message is "Command failed: git commit -m merge main into feature" — the hook's rejection text (containing 'DR-091') goes to stderr (error.stderr), which vitest's .toThrow(/regex/) does not inspect. Since the commit message arg does not contain 'DR-091', the regex never matches and this test fails in CI even though the born gate correctly rejects the commit. Sibling tests confirm the correct pattern: precommit-validate-scope.test.ts captures stdout+stderr via spawnSy…
- low packages/minspec/tests/githooks-born-gate-merge.test.ts — it('still rejects a DR born accepted in an ordinary non-merge commit') → expect(...).toThrow(/DR-092/) — This assertion passes only coincidentally: 'DR-092' is present in the commit message arg ('docs: add DR-092'), so the regex matches the echoed command rather than the gate's stderr rejection message. It does not actually verify the born gate's output; it would pass on any failure whose command happens to mention DR-092. Same fix as above — assert against captured stderr.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

commits.messageBody:
…absence from HEAD

The DR-029 born gate refused every merge-from-main into a branch older than
the most recent DR acceptance, citing DRs the founder accepted weeks ago.

Root cause: the gate selects files with `git diff --cached --name-status
--diff-filter=A`, which during a merge is computed against HEAD alone. A DR
the other parent already carries is absent from HEAD, so it reads as newly
added and is judged on its `status:` - which is `accepted`, correctly. The
gate had no way to ask whether this commit authored the file or merely
inherited it, so the false positive was systematic rather than incidental.

That is worse than a nuisance. The only documented escape is
ADR_BORN_GATE_OFF, so a gate that a correct, routine operation cannot pass
trains the reflexive override-setting that #1043 was filed to stop, and the
hook's own header records that history.

A file the commit did not author is byte-identical to one of the parents.
Only a DR whose content differs from BOTH parents was written here, and only
that one is now judged. Absence from HEAD is already implied by
`--diff-filter=A`, so only the incoming parents are checked. A conflicted
path has no stage-0 blob, so it matches nothing and stays judged: the unknown
case fails toward checking rather than past it.

T3 regression covers all three arms - the inherited DR commits cleanly, a DR
genuinely authored inside the merge resolution is still rejected, and an
ordinary non-merge commit is unaffected. Verified by mutation: blinding the
skip makes the second arm fail.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

…dy-merged fix

main independently fixed #2057 in commit 4dd2b99d (PR #2194, merged
2026-09-28), three days after this PR's own fix (6868a958, opened
2026-09-26) was written. Both hunks implemented the same behavior: skip
the DR-029 born-status check for a file whose staged blob is
byte-identical to what MERGE_HEAD already carries for that path. The
only functional difference is that this branch's version looped over
multiple MERGE_HEAD lines (octopus-merge support); main's takes the
file's content as a single parent. Every merge in this repo's actual
workflow is two-parent, so that difference is not observable here.

Resolved by taking main's side of both conflict hunks verbatim (diffed
byte-identical to origin/main:.githooks/pre-commit after resolution),
since it is the canonical, already-reviewed implementation and this
branch's copy is the superseded duplicate. Kept this branch's own new
test file, packages/minspec/tests/githooks-born-gate-merge.test.ts,
which is behavioral (execs the real hook against a scratch repo) and
adds coverage beyond what main's pre-commit-hook-behaviour.test.ts
additions already exercise. All 3 of its cases, plus all 10 in
pre-commit-hook-behaviour.test.ts, pass unmodified against main's
implementation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

…nc message

The ai-review panel flagged the two rejection-case assertions on the new
githooks-born-gate-merge.test.ts: expect(...).toThrow(/DR-NNN/) checks
the thrown Error's .message, and for a sync exec that message happens to
interpolate the command line ahead of any captured stderr. The reviewer's
"blocking" read (that stderr is never in .message at all) doesn't hold —
confirmed empirically that Node's execFileSync does append stderr to
.message on a non-zero exit — but the "low" finding is real: in the
non-merge case, the commit message argument itself contains "DR-092", so
that assertion could pass on the echoed command rather than the gate's
own rejection text, and would keep passing even if the gate's wording
changed.

Fix: switch the two commits-under-test to spawnSync + an explicit
{ok, out} pair, matching the pattern precommit-validate-scope.test.ts
already uses in this repo. `out` is stdout+stderr from the hook process
only, with no command-line echo mixed in, so a regex match can only come
from the gate's actual output. The merge-inherited-DR test's commit
message deliberately omits "DR-091" so the assertion is unambiguous.

All 3 cases still pass against the real hook; full `npx eslint .` and a
manual `tsc --noEmit` of this file (tests/ sits outside every tsconfig
include, so vitest alone never typechecks it) are both clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
